newsitem.title: USA: SEC said to meet with targets in Calif. muni probe.
newsitem.headline: SEC said to meet with targets in Calif. muni probe.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has called special meetings in Washington with targets of a municipal bond probe in California, a development that suggests the SEC may be preparing to act, sources close to the matter said on Wednesday.
The SEC was scheduling the meetings to discuss the investigation, the sources said, adding that the meetings could be the last before the SEC acts.
SEC officials in Washington and San Francisco declined to comment on the case.
The SEC investigation has focused on disclosure for the bond offerings. County and city officials said they relied on bond professionals to manage the deals.
It was not immediately clear which or how many of the local governments, firms or individuals would meet with SEC officials in Washington.

"The meetings suggest they (SEC officials) are moving closer to making decisions," said an attorney for one of the targets called to a meeting with the SEC in Washington. "They have not given us any other time frame."
Sources said other targets were also scheduled to meet with SEC enforcement officials.
As previously reported, the SEC probe has focused on Nevada County, the cities of Avenal, Wasco and Ione, underwriter First California Capital Markets Group Inc and bond attorneys.
Attorneys representing the local governments and First California either declined comment or could not be reached for comment Wednesday.

SEC staff in San Francisco sent so-called Wells notices to the local governments as well as to a number of firms and municipal bond professionals involved in deals. A Wells notice informs its recipient that the SEC staff intends to recommend enforcement action to commissioners.
